summary: Client-sent non-normalized embeddings causing suppressed rerank scores and elevated tail latency
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NoteWell reports that rerank results appear consistently suppressed (low similarity scores) and the rerank endpoint is exhibiting elevated tail latencies and occasional 503s for bulk batch requests. The customer is on a Dedicated cluster in us-east.

Impact:
- Production query throughput impacted for NoteWell search product (~5-10% traffic routed to Redwood rerank).
- p95 latency for rerank increased from ~120ms to ~2.3s for their bulk requests; p99 spikes to 6s on retries.
- Customers see degraded top-k recall and missing expected hits (low score mass).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: d-prod-wn-12 (us-east)
- SDK: notewell-internal/0.8.1 (custom wrapper) sending precomputed embeddings
- Embedding model: text-embed-3-small (client-side encoder)
- Reranker service: rerank-v2 (running on GPU with CPU fallback under backpressure)
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use NoteWell's batching pipeline to send a batch of 512 precomputed 768-d float32 embeddings to /v1/rerank endpoint with Content-Type: application/json and no normalization header.
2) Observe rerank response scores are an order of magnitude lower than same queries generated server-side with Redwood SDK defaults.
3) Repeat with SDK v1.9.3 client-side l2-normalization enabled: scores align and tail latency returns to baseline.
4) Replay customer traffic in staging against dedicated shard simulator to reproduce queued CPU normalization fallback and 503s.
logs: [2026-03-10T14:22:11Z] rerank-request id=af3b2e status=queued fallback=cpu-normalize queue_ms=1520 rt_ms=2350 -> 503
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: mismatch in embedding normalization between NoteWell's client pipeline and Redwood rerank expectations. Customer-side embeddings were not L2-normalized and did not include the optional x-embed-normalization header.

What we observed:
- Reranker assumes unit-length embeddings by default; absence of header previously routed to a legacy CPU normalization path for backward compatibility.
- Under large batches (>=256), CPU normalization caused worker saturation and queued requests; when queue depth exceeded threshold, requests hit 503s or triggered GPU->CPU fallback leading to increased tail latency.
- Score distributions showed scale collapse (values near zero) when raw embeddings had larger magnitude; after client L2-normalization scores restored.

Telemetry and dashboards:
- Trace: #support channel thread: <https://slack.redwood/#support/C055N8X1> (see thread ts 16123344)
- Grafana: rerank-p95-prod (d-prod-wn-12) jump from 120ms -> 2.3s at 2026-03-10T14:20Z
- Correlated spike with NoteWell deploy of their embedding pipeline at 2026-03-10T14:18Z

Partial repro in staging using NoteWell payloads. Attached simulated workload and scripts saved to internal S3: s3://redwood-support/repro/SUP-864210/
comments: Leah Park (Support): Reached out to customer for example payloads + sample failing request IDs. Asked for a single failing embedding vector and metadata. 2026-03-10
NoteWell SE (A. Chen): Provided batch payload and confirmed their encoder emits raw dense vectors without normalization. They were relying on server-side normalization historically. 2026-03-10
Marco Diaz (SRE): Verified CPU normalization path is single-threaded in current build; observed saturation at batch sizes >=256. Filed INT-4021 to track runtime change. 2026-03-11
Priya Nair (SDK): Provided patch in PR 2784 to add explicit header and a client-side normalization toggle in SDK v1.9.3. Asked customer to try the new SDK as workaround. 2026-03-11
NoteWell SE: Confirmed: enabling SDK-side L2 normalization normalizes scores and brings p95 back to ~140ms. Still seeing occasional 503s for historical queued requests. 2026-03-12
root_cause: Client embeddings were not L2-normalized and requests omitted the normalization header. Redwood's legacy server-side CPU normalization path becomes a bottleneck for large batches, causing GPU fallback/queueing and score scale mismatch when normalization is delayed or skipped.
resolution:
Short-term workaround: Instructed NoteWell to upgrade to Redwood SDK v1.9.3 (or apply client-side L2 normalization) which sets x-embed-normalization=l2 and pre-normalizes embeddings; this restores score ranges and eliminates CPU normalization overhead.

Medium-term fix: Engineering to harden server-side validation and fast-path: 1) Add a lightweight input validation that rejects unnormalized embeddings with an explicit error when batch size >128 (PR 2784). 2) Implement parallelized CPU normalization fallback and telemetry to avoid single-thread saturation (INT-4021). 3) Add a deprecation notice for relying on implicit server-side normalization and update docs/runbook.

Rollout plan: PRs merged to canary 2026-03-14, staged to dedicated clusters 2026-03-16, full prod rollout 2026-03-18 after performance verification.
